text:
eli_support: Hey team, customer (acme-inc) opened a ticket: tool calling fails intermittently when they proxy OpenAI-style tool calls through our API. They say it worked earlier but now 400s. Logs attached below.

mike_eng: Can you paste the request/response they send?

eli_support: Pasting sanitized request they sent (curl from customer):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/calls \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-infer","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"call tool"}],"tool_calls":[{"name":"lookup_order","arguments":"{\"order_id\":\"1234\"}"}]}'
```

eli_support: And our error in logs: 
```
ERROR 400 validate_tool_call_args: unexpected_type: expected OBJECT got STRING at tool_calls[0].arguments
payload: {"tool_calls":[{"name":"lookup_order","arguments":"{\"order_id\":\"1234\"}"}], ...}
```

anya_ml: Ah this is classic OpenAI-compat drift. The customer passed arguments as a JSON-string, but our validator expects a JSON object. OpenAI allows either in some SDKs, but our OpenAI-compat layer currently enforces object type strictly. Also ran quick grep: some of their callers also use field name `params` instead of `arguments` or `args` depending on SDK.

mike_eng: Any enum mismatches? Those have bitten us before.

anya_ml: Yes — their webhook that receives tool results returns status as `CONFIRMED` (all-caps) while our proto expects `confirmed` lowercase. Combined with stringified args, our normalizer rejects the whole call chain.

eli_support: Customer says they saw this after upgrading a client lib last week. They can repro locally and provided a minimal repro. They've asked for a quick workaround because it blocks order lookups in production.

mike_eng: Proposed short-term fixes: 1) update our request normalizer to accept stringified JSON for tool args and attempt JSON.parse if type==string; 2) add flexible enum normalizer (case-insensitive mapping) for tool result status. Both can be gated behind a per-org compatibility flag so we can roll back.

anya_ml: Agreed. I'll draft a patch for the normalizer and unit tests. Quick note: parsing arbitrary strings has security implications; limit to strings < 10k and ensure parse errors are handled gracefully.

ops-bot: Deploy pipeline triggered for branch fix/compat-toolargs (CI passed).

eli_support: Customer asked if we can hotfix their org only. Ops: can we feature-flag this by org id?

mike_eng: Yes — we have an org-level request_normalizer.flags map. I'll add `openai_compat_string_args:true` and `openai_compat_case_insensitive_enums:true` as toggles. Need a brief downtime window (config rollout across gateways) ~10m.

customer_success: I'll ask acme-inc if they can tolerate 10 minutes tonight at 22:00 UTC. If yes, I'll schedule.

anya_ml: Tests I ran locally (before patch): our validator rejects string args:
```json
{"tool_calls":[{"name":"lookup_order","arguments":"{\"order_id\":\"1234\"}"}]}
```
After my patch branch it normalizes to:
```json
{"tool_calls":[{"name":"lookup_order","arguments":{"order_id":"1234"}}]}
```
And enum `CONFIRMED` -> `confirmed`.

mike_eng: ETA for patch + canary deploy: 3-4 hours. I'll do canary in staging then prod for specific org.

eli_support: Customer is willing to test on a staging API key first. Please post the canary endpoint once ready.

ops-bot: Canary deployment completed for org acme-inc on 1863456890. No errors in initial traces.

customer_success: Acme-inc verified staging call succeeds and order lookup works. They requested we keep the feature flag on for 48h before flipping default.

mike_eng: Leaving flag on for acme-inc and adding monitoring alert to catch parse-errors or unexpected tool arg shapes.

anya_ml: Follow-up: create an internal docs blurb describing allowed tool arg shapes (object preferred, string accepted for compat) and note enum case-insensitivity behavior. I'll link PR once merged.

eli_support: Closing customer ticket after follow-up confirmation. Will reopen if anything else crops up. :white_check_mark:

mike_eng: Nice. TL;DR for the ticket: OpenAI-style clients sometimes send tool args as stringified JSON and inconsistent enum casing. We added an org-gated normalizer to accept string args (safely parse) and case-insensitive enum mapping as a compatibility shim. Long-term: recommend customers standardize on object args and consistent enums; we'll keep compat layer for 90 days then review.
